title: 📚 Past Participle (क्त)
description: Learn to use past participles to describe completed actions.

sections.title: 📖 What is the Past Participle?
sections.content: Past participles describe an action that has been completed. They function like adjectives and are often translated as '-ed' or 'having been'.

formation.rule: Add 'त' (ta) to the verb root for most verbs, 'न' (na) for some.

examples.sentence: गतः बालकः। (The boy who has gone.)
पठितं पुस्तकम्। (The book that has been read.)
खादितं फलम्। (The fruit that has been eaten.)
दृष्टो नरः। (The man who has been seen.)

usage.example: पठितं पुस्तकम् अस्ति। (The book is read / has been read.)

usage.note: Combined with 'अस्ति' to form perfect tense

usage.example: तेन पुस्तकं पठितम्। (The book was read by him.)

questions.question: What is the past participle of 'गम्' (to go)?
questions.explanation: 'गतः' (gataḥ) is the past participle of 'to go'.

questions.question: What is the past participle of 'पठ्' (to read)?
Translate: 'पठितं पुस्तकम् अस्ति।'
questions.explanation: 'पठितं पुस्तकम् अस्ति।' means 'The book is read / has been read.'
